claim: Sepsis accounts for one in three hospital deaths in the USA.
source: Sepsis accounts for one in three hospital deaths in the USA and millions of deaths each year globally, highlighting its hazard to public health (Rhee et al., 2017; Buchman et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Rhee et al., 2017 and Buchman et al., 2020

claim: Sepsis accounts for millions of deaths each year globally.
source: Sepsis accounts for one in three hospital deaths in the USA and millions of deaths each year globally, highlighting its hazard to public health (Rhee et al., 2017; Buchman et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Rhee et al., 2017 and Buchman et al., 2020

claim: The high mortality rate associated with sepsis reflects the lack of clinically viable molecular-based therapeutic target.
source: The high mortality rate associated with sepsis reflects the lack of clinically viable molecular-based therapeutic target.
evidence: This is an inference based on the current state of sepsis treatment

claim: The acute phase of sepsis is characterized by high energy consumption and hyper-inflammation associated with increased oxidation.
source: The response to sepsis has classically been characterized as a biphasic phenomenon, where the acute phase is characterized by high energy consumption and hyper-inflammation associated with increased oxidation, followed by cellular reprogramming to a low-energy, anti-inflammatory state of immunometabolic paralysis, with accompanying organ failure (Rhee et al., 2017; Osuchowski et al., 2012; Chiswick et al., 2015; Xiao et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Rhee et al., 2017; Osuchowski et al., 2012; Chiswick et al., 2015; Xiao et al., 2006

claim: The acute phase of sepsis is followed by cellular reprogramming to a low-energy, anti-inflammatory state of immunometabolic paralysis, with accompanying organ failure.
source: The response to sepsis has classically been characterized as a biphasic phenomenon, where the acute phase is characterized by high energy consumption and hyper-inflammation associated with increased oxidation, followed by cellular reprogramming to a low-energy, anti-inflammatory state of immunometabolic paralysis, with accompanying organ failure (Rhee et al., 2017; Osuchowski et al., 2012; Chiswick et al., 2015; Xiao et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Rhee et al., 2017; Osuchowski et al., 2012; Chiswick et al., 2015; Xiao et al., 2006

claim: During the early phase of sepsis, increased catabolism of fats, proteins, and carbohydrates, associated with high rates of oxygen consumption and ATP synthesis, is observed.
source: Additionally, during the early phase of sepsis, increased catabolism of fats, proteins, and carbohydrates, associated with high rates of oxygen consumption and ATP synthesis, is observed (Singer, 2014; Druml et al., 2001; Mecatti et al., 2020; Seymour et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Singer, 2014; Druml et al., 2001; Mecatti et al., 2020; Seymour et al., 2013

claim: Following the acute phase of sepsis is a hypometabolic state where ATP production and mitochondrial respiration decreases.
source: Following the acute phase is a hypometabolic state where ATP production and mitochondrial respiration decreases (Singer, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Singer, 2014

claim: The hypometabolic state during sepsis is a protective mechanism to overall lower the metabolic demands of the cell and help with its recovery.
source: It is postulated that this is a protective mechanism to overall lower the metabolic demands of the cell and help with its recovery (Lewis et al., 2016; Quinones et al., 2014; Singer et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lewis et al., 2016; Quinones et al., 2014; Singer et al., 2004, but presented as a postulate

claim: During the hyper-inflammatory anabolic phase of sepsis, an increase in the expression and activity of pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 1 (PDK1) consistently occurs.
source: Of particular interest, during the hyper-inflammatory anabolic phase of sepsis, an increase in the expression and activity of pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 1 (PDK1) consistently occurs (McCall et al., 2018; Vary, 1991).
evidence: Supported by citations to McCall et al., 2018; Vary, 1991

claim: PDK1 is one of four PDK isoforms that reversibly phosphorylates serine residues on pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (PDC) E1a subunit, inhibiting the conversion of pyruvate to acetyl coenzyme A (acetyl-CoA).
source: This enzyme is one of four PDK isoforms that reversibly phosphorylates serine residues on pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (PDC) E1a subunit, inhibiting the conversion of pyruvate to acetyl coenzyme A (acetyl-CoA) (Stacpoole, 1989).
evidence: Supported by citation to Stacpoole, 1989

claim: Inhibition of PDC is thought to be an important mechanism driving the dysfunction of mitochondrial respiration and cell bioenergetics observed during sepsis.
source: Inhibition of this important enzyme central to glycolysis, tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), and the lipogenic pathway is thought to be an important mechanism driving the dysfunction of mitochondrial respiration and cell bioenergetics observed during sepsis (McCall et al., 2018; Zhu et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to McCall et al., 2018; Zhu et al., 2020

claim: PDK serves as a potential therapeutic target as its inhibition would allow for the downstream oxidation of glucose to continue, restoring OXPHOS and mitochondrial function known to be altered in both immune and non-immune cells during sepsis.
source: Therefore, PDK serves as a potential therapeutic target as its inhibition would allow for the downstream oxidation of glucose to continue, restoring OXPHOS and mitochondrial function known to be altered in both immune and non-immune cells during sepsis (Seymour et al., 2013; McCall et al., 2018; Kelly and O'Neill, 2015; Eyenga et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Seymour et al., 2013; McCall et al., 2018; Kelly and O'Neill, 2015; Eyenga et al., 2018

claim: The liver is an important metabolic and immune organ due to its role in nutrient metabolism and production of acute phase proteins.
source: The liver is an important metabolic and immune organ due to its role in nutrient metabolism and production of acute phase proteins.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about liver function

claim: Our understanding of transcriptional alterations and subsequent metabolic phenotypes elicited by sepsis in the liver still remain limited.
source: However, our understanding of transcriptional alterations and subsequent metabolic phenotypes elicited by sepsis still remain limited (Seymour et al., 2013; Ilaiwy et al., 2019; Dahn et al., 1995; Levy et al., 1968; Han et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to Seymour et al., 2013; Ilaiwy et al., 2019; Dahn et al., 1995; Levy et al., 1968; Han et al., 2004

claim: The mechanisms by which dichloroacetate (DCA) elicits hepatic metabolic changes in response to sepsis are completely unknown.
source: Furthermore, the mechanisms by which dichloroacetate (DCA) elicits hepatic metabolic changes in response to sepsis are completely unknown.
evidence: Statement about the current state of knowledge

claim: At 30 hr post-cecal ligation puncture (CLP), septic mice exhibit tolerance, in which immunometabolic paralysis and end organ dysfunctions decrease survival.
source: At this time point, septic mice exhibit tolerance, in which immunometabolic paralysis and end organ dysfunctions decrease survival.
evidence: Based on the experimental design and prior knowledge

claim: Sepsis significantly increases the acute phase response pathway in the liver.
source: Ingenuity pathway analysis (IPA) of the top physiological pathways subject to alteration in response to sepsis revealed a significant increase in the acute phase response pathway, highlighting a persistent inflammatory state in the liver into the chronic phase of sepsis (Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by IPA analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1a

claim: OXPHOS and mitochondrial dysfunction were the top two enriched pathways in the liver of septic mice.
source: Of particular interest, OXPHOS and mitochondrial dysfunction were the top two enriched pathways in the liver of septic mice (Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by IPA analysis shown in Figure 1a

claim: Septic mice at 30 hr decreased the transcriptional output of OXPHOS components.
source: Septic mice at 30 hr decreased the transcriptional output of OXPHOS components as evidenced by a negative GSEA enrichment score (Figure 1b).
evidence: Supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 1b with negative enrichment score (NES = -0.853)

claim: Sepsis induces a negative enrichment score for TCA cycle enzymes in the liver of CLP mice.
source: In accordance with the changes observed in the OXPHOS pathway, we found a negative enrichment score for TCA cycle enzymes (GO:0006099) in the liver of CLP mice (Figure 1c).
evidence: Supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 1c with negative enrichment score (NES = -1.1956)

claim: Sepsis impairs mitochondrial metabolism in the liver.
source: Thus, our transcriptome data indicate that sepsis impairs mitochondrial metabolism in the liver.
evidence: Inference from the transcriptome data showing negative enrichment of OXPHOS and TCA cycle pathways

claim: Sepsis alters the relative abundance of multiple metabolites involved in the TCA cycle.
source: In line with altered transcriptional regulation of the TCA cycle, we found that sepsis altered the relative abundance of multiple metabolites involved in the TCA cycle (Figure 1d).
evidence: Supported by metabolomic screening data shown in Figure 1d

claim: Significant elevation of citrate was observed in septic hepatocytes at 30 hr.
source: In particular, significant elevation of citrate and cis-aconitate was observed in septic hepatocytes at 30 hr (Figure 1e,f).
evidence: Supported by UPLC-MS/MS measurements shown in Figure 1e

claim: Significant elevation of cis-aconitate was observed in septic hepatocytes at 30 hr.
source: In particular, significant elevation of citrate and cis-aconitate was observed in septic hepatocytes at 30 hr (Figure 1e,f).
evidence: Supported by UPLC-MS/MS measurements shown in Figure 1f

claim: Unlike macrophages, hepatocytes show no changes in the levels of succinate and α-ketoglutarate during sepsis.
source: Unlike macrophages, which shift their ratio of succinate and α-ketoglutarate to favor succinate accumulation over α-ketoglutarate (Liu et al., 2017; Mills and O'Neill, 2014; Mills et al., 2016), we found no changes in the levels of these metabolites in hepatocytes (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: Supported by UPLC-MS/MS measurements shown in Figure 1G,H and comparison to cited macrophage studies

claim: Macrophages shift their ratio of succinate and α-ketoglutarate to favor succinate accumulation over α-ketoglutarate during inflammation.
source: Unlike macrophages, which shift their ratio of succinate and α-ketoglutarate to favor succinate accumulation over α-ketoglutarate (Liu et al., 2017; Mills and O'Neill, 2014; Mills et al., 2016), we found no changes in the levels of these metabolites in hepatocytes (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: Supported by citations to Liu et al., 2017; Mills and O'Neill, 2014; Mills et al., 2016

claim: Unlike macrophages, levels of fumarate decreased in hepatocytes from septic animals.
source: Furthermore, unlike macrophages (Lampropoulou et al., 2016), levels of fumarate decreased, but malate levels were unchanged in hepatocytes from septic animals (Figure 1I,J).
evidence: Supported by UPLC-MS/MS measurements shown in Figure 1I and comparison to cited macrophage study

claim: Malate levels were unchanged in hepatocytes from septic animals.
source: Furthermore, unlike macrophages (Lampropoulou et al., 2016), levels of fumarate decreased, but malate levels were unchanged in hepatocytes from septic animals (Figure 1I,J).
evidence: Supported by UPLC-MS/MS measurements shown in Figure 1J

claim: Monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells reprogram the TCA cycle during acute inflammation to a catabolic tolerance phenotype by shunting cis-aconitate to itaconate through the enzymatic action of aconitase decarboxylase (ACOD1; also known as immune-responsive gene 1 [IRG1]).
source: Monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells reprogram the TCA cycle during acute inflammation to a catabolic tolerance phenotype by shunting cis-aconitate to itaconate through the enzymatic action of aconitase decarboxylase (ACOD1; also known as immune-responsive gene 1 [IRG1]) (Lampropoulou et al., 2016; Liao et al., 2019; Mills et al., 2018; Daniels et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lampropoulou et al., 2016; Liao et al., 2019; Mills et al., 2018; Daniels et al., 2019

claim: Sepsis significantly induces ACOD1 in isolated hepatocyte preparations.
source: Accordingly, we also found that sepsis significantly induces ACOD1 and elevates itaconate in isolate hepatocyte preparations (Figure 1K,L).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1K

claim: Sepsis elevates itaconate in isolated hepatocyte preparations.
source: Accordingly, we also found that sepsis significantly induces ACOD1 and elevates itaconate in isolate hepatocyte preparations (Figure 1K,L).
evidence: Supported by UPLC-MS/MS measurements shown in Figure 1L

claim: Perturbations in OXPHOS have been shown to promote the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS).
source: Perturbations in OXPHOS have been shown to promote the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) (Indo et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Indo et al., 2007

claim: Itaconate has been shown to induce activation of the master KEAP1/NRF2 antioxidant pathway leading to increased expression of redox regulatory enzymes in macrophages.
source: Furthermore, itaconate has been shown to induce activation of the master KEAP1/NRF2 antioxidant pathway leading to increased expression of redox regulatory enzymes in macrophages (Mills et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mills et al., 2018

claim: GSEA of ROS metabolism revealed a positive enrichment in livers of septic mice.

claim: Sepsis did not alter intracellular homocysteine levels in isolated hepatocytes.
source: Sepsis did not alter intracellular homocysteine levels in isolated hepatocytes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: Supported by UPLC-MS/MS measurements shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: Cystathionine decreased significantly in septic hepatocytes.
source: Sepsis did not alter intracellular homocysteine levels in isolated hepatocytes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1); however, cystathionine decreased significantly (Figure 2b).

claim: There is a trend for decreased cysteine levels in the liver during sepsis (p=0.0534).

evidence: Supported by UPLC-MS/MS measurements shown in Figure 2c with p-value provided

claim: Sepsis significantly decreased glycine in hepatocytes.
source: Furthermore, we found a trend for decreased cysteine levels in the liver (p=0.0534) (Figure 2c) and significantly decreased glycine (Figure 2d).

claim: Sepsis depleted hepatocyte glutathione.
source: Most dramatically, sepsis depleted hepatocyte glutathione (Figure 2e)

claim: Sepsis led to decreased oxidized glutathione (GSSG) in hepatocytes.
source: Most dramatically, sepsis depleted hepatocyte glutathione (Figure 2e) and led to decreased oxidized glutathione (GSSG) (Figure 2f).

claim: Ophthalmate has recently been shown to be a biomarker of oxidative stress and signals consumption of hepatic GSH.
source: Ophthalmate has recently been shown to be a biomarker of oxidative stress and signals consumption of hepatic GSH (Soga et al., 2006).

claim: Perturbations in OXPHOS, alterations in the TCA cycle, and induction of oxidative stress are metabolic hallmarks of fatty liver disease.

claim: Sepsis decreased transcriptional output of fatty acid metabolic process components in the liver.

claim: Sepsis induces alterations in genes involved in both fatty acid oxidation and fatty acid biosynthesis.

claim: Unbiased metabolomic screening in hepatocytes identified lipid metabolism as the top metabolic pathway altered in sepsis.

claim: Sepsis leads to profound accumulation of almost all lipid species surveyed.

claim: Sepsis induces significant increases in the most abundant SM species (22:0, 16:0, and 20:0) in septic hepatocytes.
